title: Sales partnership scratch notes — Nimbus Analytics
content:
Quick scratchpad for Nimbus Analytics outreach — assembling account notes, possible angles, objection handling, and email/call drafts. Most of this is TODO / rough.

Account overview:
- Company: Nimbus Analytics (founded 2017) — mid-market data & analytics platform for retail chains. HQ SF, ~450 employees. Growing SMB/enterprise customer base in NA and EU.
- Tech stack: AWS-hosted, uses Spark/Presto for analytics, experiment with vector search for product recommender. Likely using multi-cloud S3, some GCP for analytics.
- Pain signals (from news + LinkedIn + job postings): scaling inference costs for recommender/ personalization; hiring ML infra engineers; looking to reduce latency for real-time recommendations; mention of "reduce per-recommendation cost" in CTO interview.
- Likely compute: mix of CPU + gated GPU for model training; inference for recommendations currently on CPU-heavy autoscaling groups — opportunity for cost + latency wins.

Key contacts (founder/roles):
- Maya R. (CTO) — public posts about ML infra scalability. LinkedIn: maya-ramirez.
- Lukas M. (Head of ML / Director of ML Eng) — hiring for "low-latency inference" roles.
- Priya S. (Head of Product, personalization) — owns recommender roadmap.
- SDR/BD contact TBD (need to check CRM for current owner).

Why Redwood could help (hypotheses):
- Reduce per-request cost for personalized recommendations via batching + KV caching + quantization recommendations.
- Lower p99 latency with smart routing / GPU-backed serving (Dedicated or Private if data-sensitive).
- Unified infra so their ML infra team doesn't have to maintain custom serving layer — plug into Redwood Dedicated or Private.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns + regression alerts tied to evals (useful for productionizing models).

Key business metrics to probe (questions for discovery):
- Current cost per recommendation (monthly) + percent of infra budget for inference.
- Latency targets (p50/p90/p99) and SLA pain.
- Throughput: qps for peak windows (holiday, promotions).
- Model sizes & typical sequence lengths; GPU usage patterns and batchability.
- Data sensitivity / compliance requirements (do they need VPC/on-prem?).

Possible objections + suggested responses:
- Objection: "We already built our own serving layer; moving platforms is risky."
  - Response: Acknowledge. Offer migration playbook + pilot on a non-critical model (can run A/B) + can start with Hosted API or Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput. Provide case study where we replaced a homegrown stack and cut cost 30% while maintaining latency.
- Objection: "We can't expose customer data to hosted providers."
  - Response: Redwood Private with customer-managed networking + KMS integrations; emphasize audit logs + SOC2/ISO controls. Ask which data would be sensitive to map to options.
- Objection: "We're already on X GPU infra and have ops investment."
  - Response: Talk about incremental adoption (hybrid): route non-sensitive or burst traffic to Redwood, or run Redwood Private in their VPC. Highlight time-to-value and ops reduction.
- Objection: "Cost is not clear / what will it actually save?"
  - Response: Offer a lightweight cost-performance audit: send a trace + sample traffic and we'll produce a modeled estimate (expected token/req savings from batching/caching + quantization recs).

Outbound email drafts (short / long) — pick tone: pragmatic, data-driven.
- Short (cold LinkedIn / email):
  Subject: 30% cost + p99 latency wins for Nimbus' recommender
  Hi Maya — quick note: we help engineering teams (Spotify, RetailX) cut inference costs and p99 latency for real-time recommenders by 20–40% without retraining via runtime-level batching, KV caching and quantization profiles. Interested in a 20‑minute call to share a short audit of where you might see wins?
  —Jamie

- Long (first-touch email with value prop + ask):
  Subject: Pilot to reduce per-recommendation cost at Nimbus
  Hi Maya / Lukas,

  I’m Jamie on the Redwood Inference GTM team — we build an inference platform that helps product teams move from model experiments to predictable, low-cost production serving. Based on public signals (job posts + posts on infra), a couple of quick hypotheses:
  - Your recommender stack is a large fraction of inference spend and has tight latency SLAs.
  - There’s room to reduce per-request cost through batching/caching and model quantization without retraining.

  We typically run a short, 2–3 week pilot (no code changes to your model) where we ingest a representative trace and show modeled savings + p99 improvements. If useful, we can scope a canary rollout afterwards. Are you open to a brief intro call next week?

  Cheers,
  Jamie

Call intro script (first 5 minutes):
- Quick intro (30s): who I am, Redwood in one sentence (developer-first inference platform for predictable cost/latency).
- Permission to ask questions (5s).
- Confirm context (30s): "I saw you're scaling recommender infra — is that still a priority?"
- Discovery (3–4 min): focus on current infra, cost pain, recent incidents, latency SLOs, data sensitivity, and decision-makers for infra purchases.
- Close (30s): propose 2 next steps: share sample traffic/metrics for a free audit OR schedule a technical deep dive with Lukas/ops.

Metrics / artifacts to request in pilot:
- Sample latency distributions (p50/p90/p99) for recommender endpoints.
- Monthly inference cost by workload.
- Typical request payload sizes & sequence lengths.
- Current model architecture + size (if allowed).
- Any existing caching / prefix reuse stats.

Competitive notes / positioning vs alternatives:
- Compared to managed cloud endpoints: Redwood provides unified runtime + cost-aware controls and stronger production tooling (rollouts, tracing, eval regressions).
- Versus building in-house: faster time-to-value + ops reduction; vs buying inference infra vendors: Redwood focuses on developer ergonomics + observability.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Check CRM for owner and existing opp (ask Sam in RevOps). (TODO: CRM lookup by EOD 2026-02-11)
- Send short intro email to Maya + Lukas (template above) — target Wed morning. (TODO: Jamie)
- Prep pilot scope doc and cost-audit checklist — share with Priya for review. (TODO: Ethan / Priya)
- If Maya responds, schedule technical pin with Lukas + ops.

Open questions / research items:
- Any recent outages / incidents tied to recommender latency? (Search status updates / public changelog)
- Confirm if they use vector search product internally and which provider.
- What percentage of recommendations are real-time vs batch?

Notes to self:
- Keep outreach short and engineering-focused. Mention concrete metrics (p99, cost %) not marketing fluff.
- Be ready to share a one-page pilot scope and one-case-study PDF.
- If they ask about pricing, offer ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and push to audit for accurate estimate.

End of scratchpad.
